article.headline: Holdsclaw's double-double does it for Washington
article.story:
NEW YORK (AP) -- Chamique Holdsclaw had 24 points and 13 rebounds as the Washington Mystics snapped an 11-game losing streak Tuesday night with a 77-64 win over the New York Liberty. Holdsclaw scored her 1,500th career point, got her seventh double-double of the season and even dished out five assists in Washington's first win since beating San Antonio 79-72 on June 10. Annie Burgess added 15 points and Murriel Page had 11 for Washington (3-14), which tied a franchise record and dropped to the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings with the 11-game skid. Vickie Johnson scored 18 points to lead the Liberty, who lost their third in a row and dipped below .500 for the first time since losing their season opener May 31. Crystal Robinson added 15 points and Tari Phillips had 12 points and 12 rebounds. The Liberty kept the game close despite being down one key player or another most of the game. Robinson, New York's leading scorer behind injured Becky Hammon, played only eight minutes in the first half after picking up three quick fouls. She committed her fourth foul 37 seconds into the second half and immediately returned to the bench. Tamika Whitmore then went to the bench after taking an elbow in the right eye from teammate Tari Phillips, and returned midway through the period to replace Robinson, who sat briefly after tweaking her ankle. In the meantime, the Liberty, who cut the Mystics' lead to 46-45 with 11:53 to go, fell apart. New York went 4:38 without a field goal as the Mystics went on a 15-1 run. Holdsclaw dominated, dishing off when she wasn't crossing over anyone who rotated to defend her. She even led a fastbreak and passed to Coco Miller behind the back, but Miller missed the layup and Holdsclaw was called for a foul on the rebound. Holdsclaw's 3-pointer with 7:30 left put Washington ahead 61-46, and New York never threatened again. The Mystics started the second half of their season with a 9-0 run in which the Liberty looked lost on offense and defense, but the first half of the game wasn't an efficient stretch for either team. Washington committed nine turnovers to New York's eight but still managed a 22-12 lead before the Liberty cut it to 33-30 by halftime.

Game notes
Holdsclaw nearly had her double-double in the first half, scoring 11 points and grabbing seven rebounds. ... Hammon sat courtside as a play-by-play announcer during the first half. She is out for the season after tearing a knee ligament June 27.
